questions.text: Consider Verilog modules. A. One definition can have several instances. B. Parameters can configure instances at elaboration. C. Every instance must use a different source language. Which statements are correct?
Consider elaboration. A. It resolves the design hierarchy. B. It resolves parameter-dependent structure. C. Successful elaboration proves all functional requirements. Which statements are correct?

Consider traditional Verilog data objects. A. A reg declaration always guarantees a flip-flop. B. A wire represents a driven net. C. A procedural reg can model a combinational result. Which statements are correct?
Which values are in Verilog four-state logic?
options: low, high, rise and fall only.

questions.text: What does z normally represent on a Verilog net?
What does x generally indicate in a Verilog simulation?
options: A bit that must be ignored by all operators.
Always a legal physical third supply voltage.

questions.text: What is the value of the reduction OR expression |4'b0000?
What is the value of the reduction AND expression &4'b1110?
What is the value of logical AND for 4'b0010 && 4'b0100?
How many bits are in {2'b10,2'b01}?
What is {2{2'b10}}?
What unsigned decimal value does 8'h2F denote?
What is the stored 4-bit result of 4'b1111 + 4'b0001 when assigned to a 4-bit destination?
What is the signed two's-complement value of 4'b1110 when explicitly treated as signed?
Which construct continuously drives a net from an expression?
Which statement about an initial block is correct?
options: It starts once at simulation time zero for that instance.
It must repeat on every clock edge.
It always infers a clocked register.
It can contain only one assignment.

questions.text: Which behavior is described by always @(posedge clk)?
options: Execute only when clk stays low for one cycle.
Execute the block when a positive edge event occurs on clk.
Execute at every integer simulation time regardless of clk.

questions.text: Within one procedural sequence, what distinguishes blocking assignment =?
options: It always waits until the next clock cycle.
It is legal only in continuous assignments.
It never changes a variable value.
It updates before the following statement in that sequence proceeds.

questions.text: What does a nonblocking assignment normally schedule?
options: Immediate execution of a new operating-system thread.
An update for a later simulation scheduling region of the current time step.
A permanent prohibition on reading the destination.
A mandatory delay of one full clock period.

questions.text: Before a clock edge a=0 and b=1. The block executes a <= b; b <= a;. What are the updated values after nonblocking updates?
Before a clock edge a=0 and b=1. In one block a = b; b = a; executes in that order. What are the final values?
Why can two clocked blocks that communicate through blocking assignments race?
options: Every blocking assignment waits one cycle.
Verilog always sorts blocks by signal name.
A race requires a fabricated chip.
Their active-region execution order may affect the observed result.

questions.text: What does $display normally do?
options: Automatically wait until all nonblocking updates complete.
Set every unknown value to zero.
Print values when the statement executes.

questions.text: What is a useful distinction for $strobe?
options: It reports values at the end of the current time step.
It changes register values to their reset state.
It is the only way to define a clock.
It runs only after the simulation process exits.

questions.text: With `timescale 1ns/1ps, a delay #2.5 represents what nominal time?
A clock generator toggles every #5 under a 1 ns time unit. What is its period?
For a 10 ns ideal clock period, what is the frequency?
Why initialize a simulated clock before repeatedly complementing it?
options: Initialization makes the clock asynchronous automatically.
It changes all timescale declarations in other modules.
Complementing an unknown value can leave it unknown.

questions.text: Which task commonly ends a Verilog simulation?
What is the purpose of a VCD file?
options: Replace an RTL testbench with a technology library.
Record selected signal value changes for later waveform inspection.

questions.text: What does statement coverage measure?
options: Whether every possible input sequence was proved.
Whether the specification contains no omissions.
Whether every physical net is routed legally.

questions.text: What is a limitation of 100% code coverage?
options: It proves that no assertion is needed.
It proves that every manufactured chip works.
It does not by itself prove functional correctness or complete specification coverage.

questions.text: Why use a self-checking testbench?
options: It forces every design to be combinational.
It compares observed results with expected behavior automatically.
It removes the need to specify expected behavior.

questions.text: What is the role of a reference model in a testbench?
options: Supply expected results against which the DUT is checked.

questions.text: Which statement separates compilation from simulation success?
options: A design may compile while still containing functional errors.
Every syntax error is a manufacturing defect.
Simulation can run only on a physically fabricated design.

questions.text: What is the result of 1'bx === 1'bx in Verilog?
What is the result of 1'bx == 1'bx in ordinary four-state logical equality?
With sel=1'bx, what is the bitwise-merged value of sel ? 4'b1010 : 4'b1000?
What is a Verilog parameter commonly used for?
options: A mandatory register updated each cycle.

questions.text: What is a generate construct primarily used for?
options: Repeating a software computation once per simulation second.
Conditionally or repetitively constructing hardware at elaboration.

questions.text: For a task and a function in traditional synthesizable Verilog usage, which statement is appropriate?
options: A function always creates a new clock domain.
A function must contain a # delay.
A task cannot have output arguments.
A function is used as an expression and should not consume simulation time.

questions.text: What does high-level synthesis with Bambu aim to generate from a supported high-level description?
options: A silicon wafer with no downstream tools.

questions.text: Compare an HLS algorithm and its generated RTL. A. They can have different timing descriptions. B. Transaction acceptance must be interpreted consistently. C. Matching a few constant-input results proves all streaming alignments. Which statements are correct?

Consider cycle latency. A. It needs a defined input-acceptance event. B. It needs a corresponding output-valid event. C. It is necessarily equal to the initiation interval. Which statements are correct?
If an RTL pipeline produces valid outputs every 3 cycles at 100 MHz, what is its steady-state throughput?
Which statement about simulation time and wall-clock time is correct?
options: Simulated nanoseconds need not correspond to the same elapsed real time.
Faster simulation changes the specified RTL delays.
Every simulated nanosecond must take one real nanosecond.
Wall-clock speed proves the circuit frequency.
